$comment: Decision brief: what must be answered before a decision is reasonable. Each row names the tool or report that produces the answer, so nobody has to guess where to look.

answer_format_key.yes_no: a yes/no, with the date checked
answer_format_key.file: a file dropped into data/inbox/ or data/exports/
answer_format_key.choice: pick an option; the default in the last column is what happens if you say nothing
answer_format_key.account: a state you can read only while logged in

questions.question: What are the five real ASINs, and what are the products?
questions.why_it_matters: Everything monetizable, and every product claim on the site, waits on this. The supplied values are 9 characters and cannot resolve to a listing.
questions.what_we_have: Five strings and a non-Amazon host, plus a niche hypothesis from the editorial titles in the brief.
questions.missing: 10-character ASINs or the /dp/ URLs, product names, and the marketplace.
questions.where_to_get_it: Open each product page and copy the ten characters after /dp/ — or search the product in Associates Central and use the link builder (affiliate-program.amazon.com/home/productlinks/search).
questions.default_if_unanswered: Links stay locked; product fields stay blank; the site publishes buyer frameworks only.

questions.question: Does tracking ID “shopnow047c-20” exist in your Associates account, and is this site's URL registered against it?
questions.why_it_matters: A tag that is not registered to the account earns nothing and can flag the site during review. The value's shape (ends -20, 15 chars, lowercase alphanumerics) is plausible, which is all this environment can say.
questions.missing: Confirmation that it is one of your Tracking IDs and that the site URL is listed under Account Settings → Site & Channel IDs.
questions.where_to_get_it: Associates Central → Account Settings → Manage your Tracking IDs, and the Sites list.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Links are not built. No tag is printed anywhere in the site's hrefs.

questions.question: Is the account fully approved, and have the three qualifying sales in the first 180 days happened?
questions.why_it_matters: Amazon reviews the application only once three qualifying sales land (personal orders do not count), and PA-API access is offered only to accepted associates. The account state decides whether any automation of product data is possible at all.
questions.what_we_have: The published criteria, quoted in data/sources.json (SRC-06, SRC-09).
questions.missing: Your account state and the clock remaining.
questions.where_to_get_it: Associates Central home page state, and Reports → Earnings for qualifying sales.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Assume no PA-API. The collector reads pasted JSON from data/inbox/ instead of calling the API.

questions.question: Which marketplace do the links point at?
questions.why_it_matters: ASINs are marketplace-specific; amazon.com and amazon.co.uk can carry different ASINs for the same box, and commission categories differ by locale.
questions.what_we_have: The -20 suffix implies a US Store ID, so the config assumes www.amazon.com.
questions.missing: Confirmation, and the marketplace for each listing.
questions.where_to_get_it: The listing URL you copied the ASIN from; and Associates Central → Account Settings for the account's marketplace.
questions.default_if_unanswered: US marketplace assumed and labelled as an assumption in the config.

questions.question: Where will the site actually live — the Pages sub-path or a domain you own?
questions.why_it_matters: “You must own your website.” is a published review criterion, and a rejection is not re-assessed. It also decides canonical URLs, the OneLink question, and whether a click endpoint can share the origin.
questions.what_we_have: A working Pages URL and a build that takes one config line to move.
questions.missing: A domain, or the decision to stay on Pages.
questions.where_to_get_it: Your registrar, then GitHub Pages custom-domain settings.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Publish on the Pages URL as staging; do not submit it as the application property.

questions.question: Are the five products air fryers at all?
questions.why_it_matters: Sections, internal links, seasonal clusters and the whole editorial angle assume the air-fryer/multi-cooker cluster from the brief's titles.
questions.what_we_have: Four editorial hypotheses naming air fryers and multi-function appliances.
questions.missing: Product titles to file them under.
questions.where_to_get_it: The listing pages, once Q-01 is answered.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Sections keep their buyer frameworks; the five records sit in an explicit pending bucket.

questions.question: Who is the named human behind the byline, if anyone?
questions.why_it_matters: A publication needs a person who stands behind the claims; a fake expert byline is a fabricated endorsement. Until then the desk byline plus an “AI-drafted, human-edited” note is the honest state.
questions.what_we_have: Desk byline and an explicit note on every guide.
questions.missing: A real, consenting editor with a stated review scope.
questions.where_to_get_it: You, or the person you appoint; their bio and photo are the only inputs.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Desk byline stays; no credentials claimed anywhere.

questions.question: Is the brand name cleared?
questions.why_it_matters: The site prints a masthead; a name that collides with an existing mark or implies Amazon affiliation is a rename at the worst moment. Amazon's own agreement bars implying sponsorship (SRC-03).
questions.what_we_have: “The Preheat” as a working title, defined once in config.
questions.missing: A trademark search and a domain check.
questions.where_to_get_it: USPTO search plus a general search for the name in the review/publishing space; then your registrar.
questions.who: Repository owner (with counsel if it matters commercially)
questions.default_if_unanswered: Name stays, flagged as unclipped in /flagged/, and the config keeps renaming to one line.

questions.question: Where does the event endpoint run?
questions.why_it_matters: Pages is static. Click and conversion measurement needs a runtime, and the choice decides whether the site can 302 through a counter or must count client-side.
questions.what_we_have: A tested reference implementation that runs on localhost and writes day-bucketed aggregates.
questions.missing: A host: small VPS, a worker platform, self-hosted Umami/Plausible, or “none — Associates reporting only”.
questions.where_to_get_it: Your infrastructure preference and budget; the implementation is host-agnostic.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Client-side aggregate counting with the endpoint URL unset; nothing is measured until it is set.

questions.question: What is the privacy posture for anything the site collects?
questions.why_it_matters: Once a form accepts an email, or an endpoint stores a count, the site has obligations that a static page does not. Amazon's warranty section requires operating the Site in accordance with applicable law (SRC-03 family).
questions.what_we_have: No cookies, no third-party scripts, no IP retention, no live form.
questions.missing: A privacy policy statement, a processor choice if emails are collected, and double opt-in or not.
questions.where_to_get_it: Your own legal review; the inputs are the two lines above plus what the endpoint stores (see /measurement/).
questions.default_if_unanswered: Capture stays disabled and /privacy/ states that nothing is collected.

questions.question: How many hours per week will editorial actually get?
questions.why_it_matters: Cadence is the constraint on findability, and the 60-day recency expectation in Amazon's own criteria makes an abandoned site a compliance problem as well as a traffic one.
questions.what_we_have: A proposed two-per-week rhythm and a queue of titles.
questions.default_if_unanswered: One guide per fortnight, marked as a proposal in config, with the review dates that follow from it.

questions.question: Will you buy the products for first-hand use and photography?
questions.why_it_matters: It is the only route to an original opinion and original images, which is the difference between a publication and a mirror of the catalogue — and it changes what the guide is allowed to say.
questions.what_we_have: Zero testing, stated on every page. Budget question open.
questions.missing: A yes/no and, if yes, which of the five.
questions.where_to_get_it: Your budget; note that personal purchases never count toward the qualifying-sales requirement.
questions.default_if_unanswered: No testing claims; guides stay framework-led and the calculator does the arithmetic.

questions.question: How will you handle a price or availability change we cannot see?
questions.why_it_matters: Prices move daily; a stale printed price is a factual error on a page whose whole promise is being careful. There is no PA-API here, so nothing refreshes automatically.
questions.what_we_have: A decision to print no price at all, and a 90-day review interval on every guide.
questions.missing: Refresh appetite: manual quarterly, PA-API when access exists, or a “check the listing for current price” pattern permanently.
questions.where_to_get_it: Associates Central → Tools → Product Advertising API (once accepted) or the manual pattern.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Never print a price; always point to the listing and say why.

questions.question: Which path do you want this programme on — A, B, or C?
questions.why_it_matters: The three paths optimise different things and cannot all be first: polish, revenue plumbing, or traffic compounding.
questions.what_we_have: All three sequenced on /suggestions/ with exit criteria.
questions.missing: A choice, or a mixture with an order.
questions.where_to_get_it: You. If the account clock is running, B first; if the URL will be shared now, A first.
questions.default_if_unanswered: A then B, which is what this branch already ships: a real publication with the money path fully specified and locked.
